normativeBasis.interpretation: GLSL ES 1.00 reserves all identifiers containing two consecutive underscores for possible future use, and WebGL 1.0 requires shader language conformance to GLSL ES 1.00. Therefore accepting __foo or foo__bar is a GL2GPU runtime conformance failure, not a behavior that a CTS patch should normalize.

stages.name: initial-full-unmodified
stages.classificationNote: Four failures are Boolean-uniform runtime regressions. shader-with-reserved-words.html is a fifth runtime failure because GL2GPU accepts identifiers containing consecutive underscores. shader-with-double-underscore.html is classified as a contradictory fixture because it expects such an identifier to compile and its fragment shader also uses the vertex-only attribute qualifier.

stages.name: runtime-fix-targeted-unmodified
stages.scope: the six initially failing pages on Echo M4
stages.classificationNote: The Boolean-uniform fix makes four of the six targeted pages pass. The unmodified reserved-word page still exposes GL2GPU's consecutive-underscore acceptance bug, while the double-underscore page remains a contradictory fixture.

stages.name: runtime-fix-full-audited-fixture-patch
stages.scope: full locally patched suite on three systems
stages.conformanceExclusionReason: The local fixture patch removes the valid GLSL ES 1.00 checks that __foo and foo__bar must be rejected and changes the contradictory double-underscore fixture to accept the same reserved identifier class. The resulting 2864/2864 count preserves experiment lineage but cannot support a WebGL conformance-pass claim.
